jira.baseUrl.description: Your Jira site, e.g. https://acme.atlassian.net or https://jira.corp.example. On Cloud, Confluence is served from the same host

jira.deployment.description: cloud for an *.atlassian.net site, server for Data Center or Server. It decides the API version, the body format, and what a token is

credentials.token.description: Where your Atlassian token lives: a Cloud API token (id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens) or a Data Center personal access token. A reference, never the token. Used for both products; credentials.jiraToken or credentials.confluenceToken, when set, overrides it for one product

auth.mode.description: How the token is sent: basic (email:token, Cloud API tokens) or bearer (Data Center personal access tokens). auto picks basic on Cloud and bearer on Data Center

jira.authMode.description: Overrides auth.mode for Jira only, for a Jira and a Confluence on different deployments. auto follows auth.mode

jira.email.description: Overrides auth.email for Jira only; empty means auth.email

jira.defaultProject.description: The Jira project key used when no scope applies and --project is not given; empty means none

confluence.baseUrl.description: Your Confluence site. Empty on Cloud means jira.baseUrl plus /wiki; on Data Center Confluence is a separate host and must be set to use it

confluence.deployment.description: cloud or server for Confluence; auto infers it from confluence.baseUrl (*.atlassian.net is cloud)

confluence.authMode.description: Overrides auth.mode for Confluence only, for a Jira and a Confluence on different deployments. auto follows auth.mode

confluence.email.description: Overrides auth.email for Confluence only; empty means auth.email

confluence.defaultSpace.description: The Confluence space key used when no scope applies and --space is not given; empty means none

scopes.description: Named streams of work, each bound to its Jira projects and Confluence space, so commands need no --project or --space. Commands take --scope <name>, or --no-scope

defaultScope.description: The scope applied when --scope is not given; empty means no scope

fields.description: Friendly name → Jira field id, so --field points=5 works instead of customfield_10016. Ids differ per instance

people.description: Shorthand → accountId (Cloud) or username (Data Center), for --assignee dana without a user search

safety.readOnly.description: Refuse every mutating command: create, edit, comment, transition, move, delete. For an instance that is a reference source

safety.allowDelete.description: Allow deleting issues and pages (still behind --yes). false disables deletion outright

safety.allowPurge.description: Allow permanently purging trashed Confluence pages (still behind --yes). false disables it outright

defaults.issueType.description: The issue type new issues get when neither --type nor a scope says; empty means the CLI's own default

storage.exports.enabled.description: Whether pages and issues the user asks to keep are saved locally

storage.exports.path.description: Where local copies go; relative paths resolve from the repo root, ~ is home

auth.email.description: Your Atlassian account email. A Cloud API token is the password half of basic auth, so it is sent as email:token. Not a secret

label.title: Label
label.description: The name a person uses for this stream of work

projects.description: Project keys, which are also the issue-key prefixes; the first is where new issues go

labels.description: Added to issues this scope creates

jqlFilter.description: AND-ed into every search, for a slice of a shared project

parentPage.description: New pages are created under this page unless --parent says otherwise
